column2: python/gantt.py:62-91 [scope-reduction] the plan caps every render_gantt width to a 90-column budget inside the generic renderer.. scenario: existing cli or library callers that intentionally pass a larger --width or width value will silently get a narrower track, even though the bug scope is the default /implement reviewer chart wrapping on long labels.

`gantt_render_main` still uses `parser.add_argument("--width", type=int, default=default_width)`, so `args.width` is always an int and the plan's omitted-`--width` → `render_gantt(..., width=none)` path never runs on the cli. changing only the call site without updating argparse leaves default charts uncapped. if argparse is switched to `default=none` without updating validation, the existing `if args.width < 1` guard raises `typeerror` on omitted `--width`, breaking cli paths such as `test_cli_empty_stdout_when_all_rows_filtered_outside_window`. a naive argv-presence check for omission can also misclassify explicit forms like `--width=80` as omitted, silently applying the capped default path to explicit widths.
